clue.text: Some lesser vessels used for functions

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that the smaller ships are the ones put to work at official events.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that serves a purpose is used for that function; serves is the verb of usefulness.

clue.text: Awful cheat is ignoring a set of moral values

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled out of shape, so the letters of cheat is are rearranged
ignoring tells us the word a is left out of the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful cheat has no regard for a moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges CHEAT IS, and 'ignoring' drops the A from that pool, leaving CHETIS to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right conduct a person or profession holds to.

clue.text: Archdeacon over time odd cleric almost showing a bit of heart

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: odd suggests strange, so the shortened word's letters are rearranged
almost means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the word cleric written out

explanation.surface: A churchman and a peculiar clergyman somehow reveal a fragment of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CLERIC to CLERI, which 'odd' rearranges to RICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the chambers of the heart, so it is literally part of that organ.

clue.text: Ignite female anger in dispute

indicators.note: in places the female-plus-anger pieces inside the word for a quarrel

parts.note: a set-to is a quarrel or fight
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A woman's fury flares up during an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something is to make it start burning, the plain meaning of ignite.

clue.text: Plant providing bird with incentive

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
a spur is something that urges one on

explanation.surface: A plant gives a bird a reason to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering garden plant related to the delphinium.

clue.text: Exclusion of hoodlum drinking wine, hotel being put out

indicators.note: drinking means the thug takes the wine inside him

parts.note: a lout is a boorish thug

indicators.note: being put out says the hotel letter is ejected from the wine

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A thug, having drunk too much, is thrown out of the hotel and barred.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a drunk being ejected, but 'being put out' only removes the hotel letter from the wine, leaving OCK; hock is a German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockout is the exclusion of workers from their workplace by an employer.

clue.text: Review of horse coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pacer is a horse trained to a particular gait in harness racing

explanation.surface: A racing preview of a horse about to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a summary that goes back over what has happened, a brief review.

clue.text: They help people see biological group that is dying out

indicators.note: dying out says the that-is letters vanish from the group's name

parts.note: a species is a category in biological classification
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Scientists who track a vanishing species are helped by watchers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'biological group' with 'dying out' as extinction, but 'dying out' only removes IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs is informal for spectacles, the glasses that correct eyesight.

clue.text: A Parisian group let loose creating bother

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a set is a group

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters are freed to move, so let is rearranged

explanation.surface: A French gang running riot are causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or trouble them, a synonym of bother as a verb.

clue.text: Concerning certain sounds with nasty pitch — one hides

indicators.note: hides means the rearranged letters conceal the word one within them
nasty suggests the word pitch is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover from a horrible playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' sits beside 'sounds' as if musical, but it is only anagram fodder; 'nasty' makes PHTIC, which 'hides' the word one.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic describes things relating to speech sounds, such as a phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: A word leading someone to snap?

definitions.text: A word leading someone to snap?

parts.words: A word leading someone to snap?
parts.note: photographers ask subjects to say this word so they smile before the picture is taken

explanation.surface: The word that makes someone lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' suggests losing one's temper, but here it means taking a photo: the word makes the subject smile for the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying cheese shapes the mouth into a smile, the cue given just before a photograph is snapped.

clue.text: Tax setting firm back — awful riot ensues

indicators.note: ensues means the scrambled riot follows on after the reversed firm
back means the company abbreviation is written in reverse

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: awful suggests disorder, so the letters of riot are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax sets a company back and a terrible riot follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An octroi was a local duty levied on goods brought into a town, especially in France.

clue.text: Facing place by river after work

indicators.note: after puts the river behind the work
by means the place sits next to the river

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
the Po is Italy's longest river
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A spot beside a river where one turns up after the day's labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means positioned across from, which is the same as facing something.

clue.text: Lump of bread left out

indicators.note: out means the left letter is removed from the bread

parts.note: a loaf is a shaped mass of bread

explanation.surface: A chunk of bread has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lump' looks like a piece of bread, but it is the definition: a clumsy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump is a heavy, clumsy, dim person, which is what an oaf is.

clue.text: See region where there is a crooked spire

definitions.text: where there is a crooked spire

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Chester is one
a field is an area or sphere

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit an area with a church tower that leans.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESTERFIELD is a town in Derbyshire, England; its church has a famous twisted, leaning spire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield's parish church is known for its crooked spire, so the town is where one stands.

clue.text: What could be uncordial threat to cricket match?

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what unfriendly menace might hang over a game of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain cloud brings rain, which stops play in cricket, so it threatens the game.

clue.text: One no good, resentful, not very clever

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for very is dropped from the word for resentful

parts.note: envious means resentful of another's luck

explanation.surface: A worthless, bitter person who is not too bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very clever' reads as one phrase, but 'not very' removes V from ENVIOUS and 'clever' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious describes someone inventive and resourceful, a synonym of clever.

clue.text: Arrogant sort of explorer to cross African country heading off

indicators.note: to cross means the explorer's letters straddle the shortened country

parts.note: a caver explores caves

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A haughty adventurer sets out to travel across Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The explorer is not a famous name but simply someone who explores caves; 'heading off' leaves ALI for him to straddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier is a haughty, offhand person, from the dashing Royalist horseman of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Guy having self-esteem on the increase or breaking down?

parts.note: cat is slang for a man or guy
ego is one's sense of self-worth
rising means going up or increasing

explanation.surface: A man whose self-regard is either soaring or collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' suggests a collapse, but it means dividing things into classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Categorising sorts items into groups, which is analysing or splitting them up into classes.

clue.text: School sport devoid of energy

indicators.note: devoid of means the energy letter is taken away from the sport

parts.note: a game is a sport
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A school's games have lost all their vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a place of learning; here it is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A gam is a school, or group, of whales, an old whaling term.

clue.text: One church composer of a Mass at sea

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A church composer wrote a setting of the Mass on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service; here it is a floating lump.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a huge floating block of ice, a mass adrift at sea.

clue.text: Phone doctor with anger

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
bile is bad temper or anger

explanation.surface: Ringing the doctor in a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile is a mobile phone, the British term for a cellphone.

clue.text: Mineral and a resin found going back to pit

indicators.note: going back means a and the resin are written in reverse

parts.note: lac is a resin secreted by insects, used for shellac
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A mineral and some resin are discovered as one returns to the colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamine is a mineral, zinc carbonate, used in soothing skin lotion.

clue.text: Some particular goods vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: An articulated lorry carries freight by road, so it is a heavy goods vehicle.

clue.text: Contribution made by trendy place

parts.note: in means fashionable
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A donation from a fashionable venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone adds to a joint effort, their contribution.

clue.text: Singer in bank touching gold

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or bank
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A vocalist at a bank who is handling gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a financial institution, but it is the verb meaning to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor is the chief singer who leads the chanting in a synagogue or church.

clue.text: First-class hint to president

parts.note: a tip is a hint

explanation.surface: An excellent piece of advice for the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop means of the very highest quality, excellent.

clue.text: Italian writer reasoning in terms of one aspect of environment

definitions.text: in terms of one aspect of environment

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist
logic is reasoning

explanation.surface: An Italian author's thinking about the natural world.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecologic relates to ecology, the study of organisms and their surroundings.

clue.text: Great pic flogged — this tells you what has to be paid

definitions.text: this tells you what has to be paid

indicators.note: flogged suggests beaten about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine painting has been sold, and here is what it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' reads as sold, which fits the surface, but it signals rearrangement.

clue.text: The reverse of unhappy, that female seen as one going somewhere fast?

indicators.note: the reverse of says the word for unhappy is written backwards

parts.note: sad means unhappy
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman who is the opposite of miserable is seen rushing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse of unhappy' suggests happy, but it means SAD written backwards. Dasher is also one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dasher is someone who dashes, moving quickly to get somewhere.
